Highlight Clip: Patrick Witt: The U.S. Government Needs Explicit Congressional Authorization to Legally Buy Bitcoin Patrick Witt: The U.S. Government Needs Explicit Congressional Authorization to Legally Buy Bitcoin On November 10, 2026, Patrick Witt, former executive director of the White House Crypto Council, said in an interview with What Bitcoin Did that President Donald Trump is interested in adding to the government's Bitcoin holdings. The administration has discussed several ways to do so, but legal questions remain over whether the government can buy Bitcoin directly on the open market and how it could do so without triggering a negative market reaction. Witt said the administration wants to codify the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and secure explicit authorization from Congress. Because Congress controls appropriations, the administration would have to show that buying Bitcoin falls within the original purpose of any existing funds it plans to use. He added that moving prematurely could prompt Congress to insert a provision into the National Defense Authorization Act banning such purchases, undermining efforts to secure authorization. — link

Cardano Founder Hoskinson Says He Never Promised ADA Would Rise Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson said in a recent YouTube AMA that he never promised Cardano would overtake Bitcoin or that ADA’s price would rise, Decrypt reported. Responding to criticism from investors, Hoskinson said some were effectively asking him to push the token’s price higher. Hoskinson also said Cardano had completed its original roadmap, that everything he had committed to building was in place, and that the network now governs itself without relying on him. At the time of the report, ADA was trading at about $0.17, down more than 94% from its 2021 all-time high and about 86% from its 2024 peak. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $185 Million in Net Outflows, While Spot Ethereum ETFs Draw $2.36 Million in Net Inflows on November 13 (ET) According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $185 million in net outflows on November 13 (ET), marking their seventh consecutive trading day of net outflows. BlackRock’s IBIT led outflows at $144 million, followed by Fidelity’s FBTC at $41.92 million. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $2.36 million in net inflows on the same day. Fidelity’s FETH led inflows at $11.64 million, while Grayscale’s Ethereum Mini Trust ETF (ETH) saw $9.28 million in net outflows. — link
